items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: "I remember Juaro, Manuel Perez... Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez." and "them about the only three men that I knew."

ctx.x: I wondered in 1915 when you moved up here, who the best trumpet players were in the carnet, on the carnet in this city. Do you remember Oliver or Kepard or anybody like that?

I remember Juaro, Manuel Perez. I used to like to hear them men play trumpet because it takes three trumpet players to play them fumes and parades. And them too used to play the parade, you see. And both of them was loud and they could play. You see them. Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez. Now Freddie Carford, I heard him a couple of times but I don't know, he just got on out of my sight. I didn't, I never was around no place where he was playing regular. He went on away.
Did you hear Bunk Johnson? Was he here in those days?

items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: I used to hear Wind King. Wind King, I think that's his name.

ctx.x: Well, how did you get started in music yourself? Did you pick it up yourself?

I just picked it up my own self. I used to listen at these records. Wind King. I used to hear Wind King. Wind King, I think that's his name. And I wanted to learn music. So I picked that up my own self. I always wanted to blow my brothers home, but he didn't want me to blow it, you see? And blow on it, and after I found I could feel it, well, I just went on. Well, Jim Lill was the first man, stopped me out. We went down to Beuris, Louisiana, playing a carnival dance down there. Well, I couldn't play nothing. He…
I was wondering, what were those first four tunes that you played? Do you remember the first four tunes that you played?
